tip: Today, just do your three things and tick each one. That's all. Small and steady beats big and rare, because a habit you can keep on a bad morning is the one that changes how your mornings feel a month from now.

Stiff joints like warmth first. A warm shower or a heat pack for 15 minutes before you move loosens the muscles around the joint, so your first steps come easier. Warm what's stiff, cool what's swollen.

Drink a glass of water before each meal today. The cartilage that cushions your joints is mostly water, and staying well watered helps it stay soft and springy. Warm water with lemon is a nice start to the morning.

A little soreness after moving is normal. It's your muscles getting used to the work, not harm to the joint. If you're sorer than usual for more than two hours afterward, do a bit less next time. Less, not nothing.

tip: Breathe in for 4, out for 6. Do it five times. A long breath out tells your body it's safe, and tight muscles around sore joints start to let go. Try it in bed tonight too, and notice whether you settle faster.

Rest your hands in warm water for one minute, then touch your thumb to each fingertip. Warmth loosens stiff fingers and the movement keeps the joints gliding, so jars, buttons and keys come easier. Do it before the fiddly jobs of the day.
Look at your tick sheet. Every tick is a small win, and a week of them is proof you can do this. Today, reply to our check-in email and tell us which thing felt easiest, so we can build on it.

Your thigh muscles carry weight your knees don't have to. Chair stands build them. Slow is better than fast: count three up and three down. The stronger they get, the easier the sofa, the car and the stairs become.

tip: Add one more plant to one meal today. Beans in your soup, spinach in your pasta, berries on your oats. Plant foods bring fiber and natural compounds that help your body calm swelling, and one extra handful a day adds up fast.

theme: Stop while it still feels good
tip: On a good day it's tempting to do everything. Pick your amount and stop there, while you still feel good. That way tomorrow starts with energy instead of payback, and one good day leads to another.

tip: Five minutes of walking counts. So does the hallway on a rainy day. Every step moves fluid through your knees and hips, which is how those joints get fed. Walk after a meal or a warm shower, when joints are looser.

Soak soft cotton in castor oil, wrap it round your sorest joint, cover it and leave it on overnight. Test a small patch of skin first, and use an old towel because it stains. It's warm, calming, and costs very little.

Olive oil, walnuts, ground flaxseed and avocado bring the good fats your joints like. The omega-3 fats in flax and walnuts help your body keep swelling in check. Add a spoon of ground flaxseed to breakfast today.
Two weeks in. What feels a little easier than day 1? Reply to our check-in email and tell us. Your plan for the next two weeks changes to match.

theme: Kind to your joints all day
tip: Carry bags on your forearm, use two hands instead of one, and slide heavy things instead of lifting. Every bit of strain you save is energy left over for the things you actually want to do.
Hold the kitchen counter and stand with your feet close together for 20 seconds while the kettle boils. Balance gets better with practice at any age, and it means steadier steps on stairs and curbs.

Capsaicin cream comes from chili peppers. It calms the nerve signals that carry pain from the joint. A thin layer on a sore knee 3 or 4 times a day can ease pain after a week or two. Wash your hands after.
Go to bed and get up at the same time, even on weekends. A steady bedtime helps you sleep more deeply, and deeper sleep turns the pain alarm down.

Add a pinch of turmeric with a little black pepper to soup or rice, or a few slices of fresh ginger to hot water. The pepper helps your body take in turmeric's main compound, and both spices have been studied for sore joints. If you take a blood thinner, use them only after speaking with your doctor.

Ten minutes of morning daylight lifts your mood and helps your body make vitamin D. Morning light also sets your body clock, which helps you sleep better at night. Sit by a bright window if it's cold out.

tip: Three weeks of small steps. That's a habit now. Today, notice one thing your joints let you do that felt harder a month ago.

tip: Ask someone for one clear bit of help this week, like carrying the laundry upstairs. Most people want to help and just need to know how. Saving your energy for what matters to you is smart planning.

tip: Warm water for 3 minutes, cold for 30 seconds, three times, ending on cold. Switching gets the blood moving, so stiff hands and feet feel looser for a while. Move them while they're loose.
Swap one sweet thing today: cookies for walnuts and tart cherries, soda for water with lemon. A lot of added sugar can stoke swelling in the body, so small swaps add up to calmer joints over time.
A bad day doesn't undo the good ones. Do half, not nothing. Cold if hot, warm if stiff. Then build back up over a few days.
Walk with a friend, or call someone while you march in your chair. Moving is easier and more fun with company, and a plan you make with someone else is one you're more likely to keep.
Print the doctor sheet in your plan and take it to your next visit. Clear notes help your doctor help you faster.
Look at your tick sheet and your pain numbers. Reply to our check-in email and tell us what you'd like to keep, drop, and work on next.

tip: Tie each habit you want to keep to something you already do. After coffee, bed moves. After lunch, chair stands. Small hooks keep habits going.
